verses.pali: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ye keci pāṇā cattāro iriyāpathe kappenti—
verses.english: “Mendicants, whatever living creatures engage in the four postures—

verses.pali: kālena gamanaṁ, kālena ṭhānaṁ, kālena nisajjaṁ, kālena seyyaṁ, sabbe te pathaviṁ nissāya pathaviyaṁ patiṭṭhāya evamete cattāro iriyāpathe kappenti;
verses.english: sometimes walking, sometimes standing, sometimes sitting, sometimes lying down—all do so depending on the earth and grounded on the earth.

verses.pali: evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṁ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya satta bojjhaṅge bhāveti, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaroti.
verses.english: In the same way, a mendicant develops and cultivates the seven awakening factors depending on and grounded on ethics.

verses.pali: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṁ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya satta bojjhaṅge bhāveti satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaroti?
verses.english: And how does a mendicant develop the seven awakening factors depending on and grounded on ethics?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ …pe…
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant develops the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion,

verses.pali: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.
verses.english: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṁ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya satta bojjhaṅge bhāveti, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarotī”ti.
verses.english: That’s how a mendicant develops and cultivates the seven awakening factors depending on and grounded on ethics.”
